text:
Maria: FYI ran a 6h co-residency stress pass on the new allocator+kv changes, saw a new class of perf regressions and some OOM churn. attaching quick notes.
Kevin: ok can you paste the top error trace?
Maria: here — logs show repeated `OOM when allocating workspace` on model-B while model-A was idle but had large KV resident. sample: 
```
2026-03-16T03:14:22Z runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory while sizing workspace=67MB; kv_resident=1.9GB; fragmentation=~28%
```
Priya: that fragmentation number stands out. did the kernel selector fallback to conservative kernels?
Maria: yes, bench-bot reported kernel fallback at those timestamps -> fallback to kernel_v2_slow when free_contiguous < 120MB. bench-bot: `kernel_select: chosen=conv_gemm_kernel_v2_slow (fallback, contig_req=128MB, avail_max_block=96MB)`
Sam: so we have two things colliding: large KV cache footprint that doesn't shrink fast enough + kernel choices that want large contiguous workspace. When they co-reside on a single GPU we get splits and OOMs.
Kevin: what about preemptible KV eviction? we talked about a grace window but maybe it's too long. how long is current ttl?
Maria: currently 300s idle TTL before eviction. during the test model-B spikes and needs workspace within <10s. TTL too conservative for multi-tenant hotspots.
Priya: proposal: soft-slotting VRAM into three bands: "hot workspace" (low-latency kernels), "warm KV" (evictable with short notice), "cold KV" (long-lived). allow dynamic reclaim of warm KV with notification and async spill.
Sam: +1. Implementation sketch: maintain per-model warm_score; when allocation request fails, try to reclaim warm KV LRU across co-resident models with warm_score < threshold. If still fail, escalate to cold -> spill to NVMe.
Maria: also observed kernel selection policy is too binary: picks single kernel based on global contig_max metric. Suggest adding kernel-sensitivity scores for fragmented environments that prefer streams with smaller working set even if slightly slower.
Kevin: that aligns with batching heuristics idea: prefer batch packing that reduces max_seq in the batch to shrink workspace if it prevents OOMs. trade a bit of throughput for fewer regressions. we could expose knob `batch_oom_avoidance=true` per-hostpool.
Priya: here's a tiny pseudocode for the eviction priority we tested: 
```
# on alloc failure req_size
candidates = collect_kv_segments(sorted_by: (warm_score, last_access))
reclaimed = 0
for seg in candidates:
  if seg.warm and seg.warm_score < reclaim_threshold:
    reclaimed += seg.size
    async_evict(seg)
    if reclaimed >= req_size: break
if reclaimed < req_size: escalate_to_spill_or_preempt()
```
Sam: We should also instrument a new metric: contiguous_block_max_by_age and expose flamegraphs for per-allocation. bench-bot: I pushed a patch that samples `max_contig_block` after every large allocation (>=16MB).
bench-bot: SUMMARY: 6h run: 42 allocation fallbacks, 7 soft-evictions triggered, 3 NVMe spills. avg latency delta when fallback kernel used: +18ms/token for model-B.
Maria: actionable checklist: 1) reduce warm TTL from 300s -> 30s for dense multi-model hosts (config flag) 2) implement warm_score-based async reclamation 3) add `batch_oom_avoidance` packing policy and server-side guardrail to prefer batches that cap per-request workspace 4) kernel selector: add "fragmentation-aware" scoring to penalize kernel with high contiguous requirement 5) dashboards: contiguous_block_max_by_age, warm_kv_evictions, fallback_kernel_count.
Kevin: also add an emergency preempt policy: if high-priority model requests and we are at >90% VRAM, preempt lowest-priority warm KV segment immediately (no TTL). we can gate behind a config.
Priya: one caveat — aggressive eviction spikes NVMe IO; recommend rate-limit async evictions to <200MB/s and add a backoff if spills >2/min.
Sam: can one of you draft a small e2e benchmark that simulates: 2 models (long-context KV heavy) + 1 spikey short model and measure: OOM count, fallback_kernel_count, avg token latency. I'll wire it into the nightly perf-run.
Maria: I'll draft it and include an argset for `fragmentation_level` to simulate different allocation patterns.
Kevin: plan LGTM. assign owners: Maria -> reclamation impl & TTL flag; Priya -> kernel selector scoring; Sam -> e2e harness + dashboard panels; I'll add the emergency preempt flag and run a long overnight.
Priya: tiny follow-up: we should log preemption events with stack: which model, reclaimed bytes, time-to-alloc-success. important for troubleshooting.
Maria: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy started: feature/soft-slotting-reclaim (canary to pool-3)
Maria: tagging this thread for postmortem if canary shows regressions.
Kevin: thanks — will monitor tonight and post quick summary in morning.
